title: Choose Hisaab's new look
question: The roll assigned Rate Board. Keep it, take my pick, take the standard look, or re-roll.

options.label: Rate Board
options.lineage: Hand-painted Indian shop boards and chai-stall rate lists
options.thesis: Every group reads like a painted rate board: names and amounts lettered big and plain, nothing boxed.
options.viewport: A solid ultramarine board across the top carries the screen name in condensed yellow lettering and your overall balance painted large; below it groups run as a rate list, name left, amount right, split by painted rules; one yellow Add expense button sits at thumb height.
options.risk: If the lettering is timid it reads as a plain blue header; if pushed too far it turns into a kitsch truck-art costume.

raised.raise: One flat colour field owns the top of every screen, no tints, shading or gradients.
Motion is hard steps: state changes swap in under 100ms, nothing fades, floats or eases on hover.
Sections are divided by painted rules, never wrapped in rounded cards.
Every expense carries its bill number in sequence, like a shop's bill book.
Every amount sits in one right-aligned tabular column, so rupees line up down the screen.
Settle up shows one payment at a time at full scale, the next one waiting below.

options.label: Scoreboard
options.lineage: Manual cricket scoreboards at grounds and college fests
options.thesis: The group is a match in progress: a green scoreboard shows who is up and who still owes, in big plate numerals.
options.viewport: A bottle-green board fills the top with the overall balance as hung number plates; below, the groups are listed like a batting order with each one's standing; one Add expense button at the bottom.
options.risk: Very familiar idea in India, so it can read as a cricket theme; the green board also competes with the get-back green.

options.label: Guide Map Lobes
options.thesis: Each balance as a swelling lobe of flat colour on a cream map.
options.viewport: One green lobe swells across the screen holding the balance.
options.risk: Playful and childish for money between friends.
options.case: Fuses poorly: friends in India do not see their hisaab as a park map, and lobes blur exact amounts.
options.kept: Flat colour committed at region scale, one field per screen.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.lineage: Reels and Shorts style full-screen feeds
options.thesis: One expense fills the screen, the next one flick away.
options.viewport: A single expense full screen with actions stacked on the right.
options.risk: You cannot scan a group's balances one screen at a time.
options.case: Familiar to the audience but loses on clarity: balances need a list, not a feed.
options.kept: One complete thing at a time, used for settle up.

options.label: Acetate Manual
options.lineage: Boxed software manuals with tab dividers
options.thesis: Each group a coloured tab section with acetate leaves.
options.viewport: A stepped tab rail of groups down the right edge.
options.risk: Reads as a novelty object, not a money tool.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no link to how friends in India keep hisaab.
options.kept: Stepped, instant motion with no easing.

options.label: High-Density Modules
options.thesis: Dozens of small ruled modules packed on one screen.
options.viewport: A mosaic of tiny boxed modules with red tabs.
options.risk: You said dense and cramped feels wrong.
options.case: Fuses poorly: too dense for adding an expense one-handed.
options.kept: A strict rule system instead of cards.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Every item numbered, colour codes instead of words.
options.viewport: A black screen with one white line plot and a catalog number.
options.risk: Black ground and hidden labels; codes instead of words hurt clarity.
options.case: Fuses poorly: money needs words, not codes.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: Pure black and white barcode fields of numbers.
options.viewport: Columns of monospace numbers over barcode stripes.
options.risk: Cold and unreadable for non-technical friends.
options.kept: Tabular numerals in one strict column.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What expense splitters ship, done very well: white list rows, avatars, a green and orange balance line.
canonCard.viewport: Overall balance as a line of text, groups as avatar rows, a floating Add expense button.
canonCard.risk: Looks like Splitwise by design, the same as every other app in the category.
